newsitem.title: CHINA: China exports ostriches -- to hungry North Korea.
newsitem.headline: China exports ostriches -- to hungry North Korea.

text.p: China's infant ostrich industry has begun exporting birds to famine-threatened North Korea, newspapers and breeders said on Wednesday.

The Beijing Shoujia Ostrich Breeding Centre on March 27 sent 21 African ostriches on a special flight to North Korea as part of a deal with a trading company in the Stalinist hermit nation, the Market Daily said.
Aid workers say North Korea, which has seen food stocks slump after years of natural disaster and economic decline, could be just weeks from widespread famine.
"I'm not sure what they want (the ostriches) for," said an official at the Beijing breeding centre.
Ostrich meat is still an expensive rarity in China, but a number of companies are busily breeding birds in the hope that it could one day become a staple.
The Beijing breeding centre already had 500 ostriches, although it was still developing the flock and was not selling any for food, the official said.
